Hi all — I completed a preliminary trace with our bank and attached the PDF with payor trace details (bank-trace-neo-0422.pdf). Summary below: 

- Payment A: EUR 38,425.00 (posted 2027-04-20 02:13 GMT) 
  - Trace: BTX-NEO-7745123
  - Bank notes: "NW-INV-202704" truncated; appears to correspond to invoices INV-2027-0421 and INV-2027-0422 (split allocation).
  - No VAT withheld on this leg.

- Payment B: EUR 8,300.00 (posted 2027-04-20 02:28 GMT) 
  - Trace: BTX-NEO-7745124
  - Bank notes: "NW-CK-" — appears to be an internal adjustment/fee OR PO-related clearing; bank shows an implied withholding flag for NL domestic bank (we're seeing a net amount).

Proposed posting (provisional):
- Apply Payment A against INV-2027-0421 (EUR 26,750) and INV-2027-0422 (EUR 11,675) respectively (full match).
- Apply Payment B as a partial credit to INV-2027-0423 (EUR 12,500 outstanding) for EUR 8,300 and leave a small unapplied balance on that invoice.

Accounting note: if Payment B was net of local withholding, we need the withholding certificate or bank advice to book the tax receivable and potentially issue a credit or claim refund. I've attached a one-line journal to temporarily record the withheld amount pending evidence.

Attachments: bank-trace-neo-0422.pdf (stub)

- We initiated two transfers on 2027-04-19 from our Amsterdam virtual pool. The payments were split intentionally: one for vendor invoice coverage, one to settle an outstanding vendor credit. 
- Payment A (BTX-NEO-7745123) was gross and should map to INV-2027-0421 and INV-2027-0422 as you identified.
- Payment B (BTX-NEO-7745124) was a net payment; our bank withheld a local tax of EUR 2,100 before crediting Redwood (they flagged as "withholding - domestic bank"). We have attached the bank advice stub (neowave_bank_advice_0426.pdf) showing the withholding code and the gross amount.
